flags.title: Non-Expansion — Smallest State Population, Thinnest FQHC Network
flags.summary: Wyoming has NOT expanded Medicaid and has the smallest state population (~577K) with the thinnest FQHC network in the country. Coverage gap for non-categorical adults is severe. Wyoming Primary Care Association: 307-632-5743 / wypca.org. Community Health Centers of Central Wyoming: 307-233-6000.

flags.title: Wind River Reservation — Two Tribes (Eastern Shoshone + Northern Arapaho)
flags.summary: The Wind River Reservation is unique as the only reservation shared by two distinct tribes: Eastern Shoshone and Northern Arapaho. Each has separate governance and social services. Eastern Shoshone: 307-332-3532. Northern Arapaho: 307-856-6117. IHS Fort Washakie: 307-332-9400. Wind River Legal Services: 307-856-9666.

flags.title: Smallest Legal Aid Infrastructure — Wyoming Legal Services Only Statewide Provider
flags.summary: Wyoming has the smallest legal aid infrastructure in the country. Wyoming Legal Services is the ONLY statewide legal aid provider. Capacity is extremely limited. Wyoming Legal Services: 877-432-9955 / wyominglaw.org. 1017 E Main St, Riverton, WY 82501.

flags.title: Energy Boom-Bust Economy — Income Verification Timing Critical
flags.summary: Wyoming's economy is heavily dependent on oil, gas, and coal. Boom-bust cycles cause dramatic income swings. Income verification timing is critical for benefits eligibility — a client may qualify during a bust but not during a boom. Document income carefully with attention to seasonal variation.

flags.title: UI 10-Day Appeal Deadline — Among Shortest in Registry
flags.summary: Wyoming UI appeal deadline is 10 days — among the shortest in the registry. Contact legal aid within 5 days of any denial. WY DWS: 307-473-3789 / wyomingworkforce.org.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: Wyoming Emergency Detention
flags.message: WY involuntary psychiatric hold law: Wyoming Emergency Detention. Statutory authority: Wyo. Stat. § 25-10-109. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in WY retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in WY: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Wyoming Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Wyoming Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
